column3: The Hebrew addresses his soul and says there is no salvation for him in God; BSB says God will not deliver him.
The Hebrew presents His answer as a completed action; BSB says answers.
The Hebrew presents lying down, sleeping, and waking as past actions; BSB uses the present.
The Hebrew says You have struck and broken, with for; BSB makes both commands.
The Hebrew leaves the blessing clause without a verb; BSB supplies may be.
